item.title: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.03881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kramers theorem generally guarantees the spectral degeneracy of time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operators with half-integer spin, underlying a variety of physical phenomena. Despite its fundamental significance, the Kramers degeneracy has been argued to be absent in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states because of the double structure of the Hilbert space. Here, we instead demonstrate that the interplay of time-reversal symmetry$^{\dag}$ and parity symmetry enforces the Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillians. We explicitly construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins exhibiting the Kramers degeneracy and show that their complex spectral statistics follow those of non-Hermitian random matrices in the corresponding symplectic symmetry classes. Of the three fundamental universality classes of non-Hermitian random matrices, the symplectic class has never been realized in symmetry-resolved many-body Liouvillians. Our constructions provide its explicit realizations and spectral signatures of nonintegrability in symplectic open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Kawabata

item.title: Energy-Resolved Cross-Correlation of THz Field Emission of Electrons from a Metal Nanotip
item.description: arXiv:2611.04036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intense THz pulses, combined with the lightning-rod field enhancement at metal nanotips, can drive field emission of keV-energy, femtosecond-duration electron bunches, yet the dynamics governing this emission remain largely unexplored. Here we probe these dynamics by cross-correlating the energy-resolved emission driven by two independently generated single-cycle THz pulses focused onto a tungsten nanotip, scanning their relative delay over 160 ps. At total bunch charges approaching $10^6$ e$^-$, the delay-energy emission map near zero delay reveals electrons accelerated up to 2.1 keV, with a cross-correlation width of ~210 fs full width at half maximum at the highest energies. Apart from replicas caused by optical reflections in the setup, no emission echoes are observed over the full delay range, ruling out long-lived antenna resonances such as Sommerfeld-wave reflections along the tip shaft. A 1D Fowler-Nordheim model incorporating a low-$Q$, sub-picosecond antenna response for the local field enhancement reproduces the peak electron energies and the asymmetry of the delay-energy map. Our results indicate that each THz pulse produces a single, isolated electron burst, and that energy filtering can select its shortest, highest-energy component.
item.dc:creator: Laurent N. David, Rodrigo T. Paulino, Angela Moskal, David G. Cooke

item.title: Chirality rules for optical vortices in rhombohedral graphene multilayers
item.description: arXiv:2611.04076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical zeros are momenta where the interband dipole vanishes. The dipole phase winds around each of them by an integer, so they are vortices of the resonant optical response with a conserved charge. We show that in rhombohedral graphene multilayers one integer, the stacking chirality $N$, fixes their constellation near the $K$ valley: the total charge per linear polarization is $N-1$ and is conserved under trigonal warping and interlayer bias; for $N\ge3$ the $K$ point stays an exact optical zero, the Bernal bilayer being the only exception; warping places the remaining charge on satellites whose radii scale linearly with the warping; and the charge pinned at $K$ is bias independent for $N\ge4$. A quantized interband character counts the enclosed charge as an integer staircase with steps at these radii, and an interlayer bias drives a satellite through the protected $K$ vortex in the trilayer. The rules survive the remote hoppings of the full tight-binding model and, being integer charges, the corrections that reshape the bands. The same integer sets the magnitude of the response: the band-edge shift current grows linearly with $N$.
item.dc:creator: Felipe P\'erez Riffo, Mat\'ias Castro Schnaidt, Juan M. Florez, Eric Su\'arez Morell

item.title: Anomalous Hall Response and Real-Space Current Correlations in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.04312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and magnetization observed in rhombohedral graphene through real-space calculations which lead to new insights. Our calculations reveal no equilibrium loop currents of the type associated with the Haldane model of a quantum anomalous Hall insulator. Instead, the AHE arises in this instance from interference between electronic paths forming oriented closed Wilson loops of current operators in the presence of valley polarization. We show some examples of these Wilson loops. Using the fact that the added-carrier charge density resides dominantly in the top and bottom layers, we develop a real-space expansion of the surface Hamiltonian that reproduces the Hall response of the full model with good accuracy. We also predict that a smooth local potential induces equilibrium circulating currents whose strength depends on both Berry curvature and the orbital moments of states at the Fermi surface.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Bi, Chandra M. Varma

item.title: Altermagnetism-induced higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an altermagnetism-induced route to a two-dimensional higher-order topological Dirac semimetal in a trilayer nonsymmorphic Dirac system. Interlayer hybridization preserves the nonsymmorphic bulk Dirac crossings and generates helical edge states in the trilayer phase. Introducing outer-layer $d$-wave altermagnetic order gaps the helical edge states, while only the symmetry-protected Dirac crossing at high-symmetry point $M$ remains gapless. The resulting phase hosts a surviving bulk Dirac point, gapped edge spectra, and corner states. An exact layer-space decomposition further reveals that these features arise from the coexistence of a gapless Dirac sector and a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological sector. Our results establish altermagnetism as an effective mechanism for engineering higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.
item.dc:creator: Lizhou Liu, Cheng-Ming Miao, Ying-Tao Zhang, Qing-Feng Sun

item.title: Dissipationless valley diode effects in Kekul\'e graphene superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.04396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting diodes have attracted considerable interest for nonreciprocal device applications owing to their dissipationless transport. Here, we theoretically propose that a tunnel junction based on the Kekul\'e graphene superlattice can host a finite valley supercurrent that exhibits pronounced nonreciprocity even in the absence of superconductivity, giving rise to a dissipationless valley diode effect. This effect originates from the additional reflection phase acquired by electrons in each transverse channel and supports perfect valley diode rectification with $100\%$ efficiency, which can be readily tuned via the gate voltage. This finding provides a platform for designing dissipationless valleytronics in a more versatile manner.
item.dc:creator: W. Zeng

item.title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.04752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons. These results establish engineered system-bath coupling and nonlinear interactions as a route to suppress dissipation of chiral topological edge transport.
item.dc:creator: Bhoomija Chaurasia, Sebabrata Mukherjee

item.title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the transport properties of a topological insulator (TI) connected to two-dimensional altermagnetic (AM) leads in the absence of an external magnetic field. Exploiting the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking of altermagnets, we report the emergence of a field-free transverse differential conductivity in the resulting AM-TI-AM heterostructure. Our analysis reveals that this transverse response is highly sensitive to the orientation of the N\'eel vector: a finite transverse conductivity manifests when the N\'eel vector possesses an out-of-plane component, whereas it strictly vanishes for in-plane orientations ($\theta = \pi/2$) under symmetric chemical potentials ($\mu_t = \mu_b$) due to the restoration of symmetry between the $k_y$ and $-k_y$ momentum channels. Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($\mu_t \neq \mu_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane N\'eel vector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while the longitudinal differential conductivity exhibits Fabry-P\'erot-type oscillations as a function of the TI's chemical potential, the transverse conductivity displays a distinct antisymmetric dependence. Notably, the oscillatory behavior of the longitudinal conductivity persists even at finite temperatures. Spatially, the transverse current contribution decays exponentially with position inside the TI region. We also find that both the longitudinal and transverse differential conductivity exhibit periodic oscillations with the junction parameter $\chi_t=\chi_b$. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of field-free transverse responses in spin-momentum locked boundary states, highlighting the potential of AM-TI heterojunctions for next-generation spintronic applications.
item.dc:creator: Bijay Kumar Sahoo, Abhiram Soori

item.title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.04938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geometric phase acquired by low-energy quasiparticles encircling defects in graphene. Following Anandan, this phase is the holonomy of the Poincare connection; its translational part couples momentum to torsion, giving $P_a\int T^a$. In the Katanaev-Volovich theory, dislocation torsion is confined to the defect core. For graphene, the relevant momentum is $\hbar(\tau_3\KK+\mathbf q)$. We show that an isolated dislocation yields a topological valley factor $e^{\mp2\pi i/3}$ when its Burgers vector $\bb$ lies outside the $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3$ superlattice, together with a dispersive factor $e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\bb}$ for every nonzero $\bb$. The topological factor recovers the lattice result of Mesaros et al. as a torsion-flux phase; 4-8 dislocations retain only the dispersive contribution. Composing Volterra elements gives the holonomy of defect complexes. At zero net Frank angle, it depends only on the net Burgers vector. The valley flux obeys a three-coloring rule: pentagons and heptagons contribute according to their Kekule site color, whereas squares and octagons do not. Atomic models confirm that ring content alone does not fix the phase: a 5-8-5 core is invisible as a divacancy or as a dislocation with $|\bb|=\sqrt3a$, but carries flux $\pm1/3$ for $\bb=2\mathbf a_1$. The torsion trace produces no geometric phase: its vector coupling violates time-reversal symmetry, while the allowed axial coupling causes only anisotropic short-range scattering.
item.dc:creator: G. Q. Garcia, A. M. de M. Carvalho, C. Furtado

item.title: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2611.04996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

item.title: ConvexAD: differentiable phase retrieval with geometric regularization for high-strain, low-signal Bragg coherent diffraction imaging
item.description: arXiv:2611.05020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging (BCDI) relies on phase retrieval (PR), a non-convex, ill-posed inverse problem whose conditioning is degraded by factors like noise, partial coherence, and strain or crystallographic defects in the imaged nanocrystal. Conventional approaches, including alternating projections and deep learning methods, represent the object on a dense voxel grid, which is prone to amplitude-phase mixing and becomes increasingly ill-posed under these factors, often preventing reliable three-dimensional mapping of the particle's shape and strain. Here we present ConvexAD, a gradient descent PR model that parametrizes the object shape as a convex polyhedron, built by the intersection of half-spaces and enforces flat amplitude within it by construction. This geometric regularization eliminates amplitude-phase mixing and reduces the number of trainable parameters, hence facilitating the convergence of the PR. Implemented in JAX for native GPU acceleration and forward-model flexibility, ConvexAD is validated on simulated and experimental BCDI data, where it outperforms conventional and deep learning assisted PR at high strain, low signal, and reduced coherence, extending the conditions under which quantitative BCDI reconstruction is achievable.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Masto, Ewen Bellec, Etienne Polack, Jiangtao Zhao, Vincent Favre-Nicolin, Steven J. Leake, Tobias Sch\"ulli, Marie-Ingrid Richard

item.title: Twisting the pseudo-magnetic field lattice in periodically strained Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.05122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic deformations flatten electronic bands of graphene which could host strongly correlated electrons similar to those observed in twisted graphene bilayers. The most spectacular effects of strong correlations like superconductivity or magnetism have however not yet been observed despite several experimental attempts. Here, we use tight-binding calculations to investigate the effect of twisting the periodic strain lattice with respect to the atomic lattice. We find that misaligning the two lattices kills the band flattening. We also report on the universal behavior of the band flattening by periodic strain which is controlled by a single parameter, a pseudo-magnetic field flux. Our study strongly suggests that controlling the twist of the strain lattice is essential to unlock the potential of periodic strains in graphene.
item.dc:creator: L-M. Benneka, T. Rhouma, C. B. Winkelmann, M. Zelzmann, G. Trambly de Laissardi\`ere, V. T. Renard

item.title: A Resonant-Tunneling Quantum-Dot Demultiplexer for Scalable Cryogenic Single-Electron Routing
item.description: arXiv:2611.05194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling quantum electronic systems such as quantum-dot spin qubits and single-electron devices is increasingly limited by the wiring overhead between cryogenic devices and room-temperature control electronics. Multi-channel quantum-dot architectures that selectively route electrons using a few shared control lines, analogous to demultiplexers in classical networks, offer a promising solution. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a gate-defined architecture of three parallel quantum dots sharing a common source reservoir and coupled to independent drain channels. Using an analytical electrostatic model and tight-binding quantum transport simulations, we show that the device can act as an on-chip single-electron demultiplexer based on resonant tunneling in the cryogenic regime. Closed-system eigenstate analysis reveals localized orbital states in each dot, and open-system transport calculations show resonant conductance peaks when these levels align with the incident electron energy, consistent with the closed-system eigenenergy evolution. By engineering the barrier-gate spacing and the relative plunger-gate dimensions, we obtain well-separated resonances with minimal overlap between channels. Bond-current density calculations show that transport is confined to the resonant channel with negligible leakage into neighboring outputs, yielding channel selectivity approaching unity for all resonant modes. The architecture is compatible with Si/SiGe and GaAs/AlGaAs platforms and can be extended to more channels, offering a route toward programmable quantum routing and resonant-tunneling-based quantum circuitry.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Bharadwaj, Harshita Bose, Madhu Thalakulam

item.title: Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$_3$ via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.03978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.
item.dc:creator: Dongwon Shin, Xiyou Peng, Kaleb McClure, Paolo Vilmercati, Chris Howard, Petro Maksymovych, Norman Mannella, Hanno H. Weitering, Wonhee Ko

item.title: Continuum Dirac Theory and Nonlinear Extensions of a Chain of Alternating non-linear springs: an SSH version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model
item.description: arXiv:2611.04049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A mechanical version of the SSH model, made of equal masses joined by two alternating non-linear springs is studied in the continuum limit. Such a non-linear dimerized mechanical chain generates a nonlinear, dispersive, two-field hyperbolic system of Boussinesq type of differential equations, describing coupled acoustic and gapped optical fields. The corresponding Lagrangian density is found, revealing that the acoustic and optical degrees of freedom are coupled through a structure that is formally analogous to a synthetic spin-orbit coupling, where the spatial motion is locked to the internal sublattice degree of freedom. An emergent non-Abelian Berry connection term also appears. Some particular solitary-wave solutions are found using variational theory, as the effective optical field obeys an undamped and unforced cubic-quintic Duffing equation. Near the Brillouin-zone edge, the system becomes a nonlinear Dirac field theory of the Soler type, providing a direct mechanical realization of interacting relativistic solitons. By factoring out fast spatial oscillations, an effective Jackiw-Rebbi Hamiltonian is obtained, with topological zero modes at domain walls. These modes are akin to the electronic flat bands in moire graphene systems associated with superconductivity and charge fractionalization. Finally, we discuss the mechanical rigidity transition and its effects on the fields as the system evolves toward the fully dimerized limit, in which the zero modes are floppy modes.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo G. Naumis, Ilder I. Salgado, Jorge Fujioka

item.title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.
item.dc:creator: Laurenz Kremeyer, Bradley J. Siwick, Samuel Huberman

item.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness, in-plane homogeneous, in-plane isotropic layer with a general nonlocal susceptibility, using a single-scale asymptotic expansion in $\eta = l\max(k_0,q)$, where $l$ is the layer thickness, $k_0$ the free-space wavenumber and $q$ the in-plane wavenumber. The sheet limit must be taken after resumming the out-of-plane depolarizing field, as this ensures that the resulting sheet susceptibility is independent of the material thickness. The arithmetic mean then emerges as the leading-order polarizing field for general susceptibility profiles. Asymmetries in the layer profile modify the effective susceptibility appearing in the transition conditions, rather than altering the arithmetic-mean field prescription. If the spatial profile is not even in both out-of-plane coordinates, in-plane and out-of-plane response hybridize, turning the diagonal volumetric susceptibility into a $q$-dependent effective tensor surface susceptibility with off-diagonal components. Mirror symmetry alone does not remove this hybridization. Comparison with exact solutions for local and separable layers shows that the derived conditions remain accurate to $O(\eta)$ across propagating and evanescent excitations, whereas the standard sheet conditions fail once hybridization becomes appreciable.
item.dc:creator: Asbjorn Hansen

item.title: Spin-Density-Driven Hybrid Spin Splitting in Collinear Compensated Magnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.04617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated magnets is constrained by spin-group symmetry, with distinct alternating and Zeeman-type splitting typically associated with altermagnets and fully compensated ferrimagnets, respectively. From a spin-density perspective, we propose a class of hybrid compensated magnets in which alternating-like and Zeeman-type spin splitting coexist within a single collinear compensated state. Using a minimal two-sector model, we demonstrate that this coexistence arises from competition between directional sublattice dispersion and the sector-dependent energy biases arising from the same structural inequivalence. First-principles calculations provide a proof of concept in a crossed bilayer of unequal-width Janus graphene nanoribbons, where the structurally inequivalent ribbons retain approximately symmetry-related spin-density distributions. The valence and conduction sectors support direction-selective spin transport and energy-selective spin-polarized states, respectively. These results connect the spatial organization of spin density with the electronic response to structural inequivalence, providing a design principle for hybrid spin splitting in compensated magnets.
item.dc:creator: Peibo Xu, Yixuan Che, Yuxuan Li, Haifeng Lv, Xiaojun Wu, Jinlong Yang

item.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
item.description: arXiv:2611.04729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. The Curie temperature depends crucially on the compensation degree. Depending on Mn content and compensation degree, three possible magnetic phases (paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and spin-glass-like) are predicted. However, the spin-glass-like phase in (Ga,Mn)As is apparently not realized due to the additional inevitable compensation caused by As antisites. The phase transition into the ferromagnetic state occurs not only with Mn content variation but through the change of the compensation degree as well. The new mechanism of photoferromagnetic effect is predicted and discussed in the context of possible clarification of the magnetic ordering mechanism. It is assumed that the main obstacle to a possible increase in the Curie temperature is the increasing contribution of the antiferromagnetic superexchange between the nearest-neighbor Mn's, rather than compensatory (electric or magnetic) effects from Mn interstitials, as was previously stated. The comparison of our predictions with available experimental data is presented.
item.dc:creator: I. A. Kokurin, N. S. Averkiev

item.title: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities
item.description: arXiv:2611.05185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.
item.dc:creator: Hao-En Li, Zhen Huang, Lin Lin

item.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $\lambda_c$ from the classical value $2\pi r_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $\lambda_c<2\pi r_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $\lambda_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Khenner

item.title: Photoinduced topological phase transition in monolayer 1T$^\prime$-MoS$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2511.15268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the systematic competition between perpendicular electric field and circularly polarized light in nonequilibrium topological phases of monolayer 1T$^\prime$--MoS$_2$ using a low-energy $k\!\cdot\!p$ Hamiltonian and Floquet theory. The off-resonant field generates spin- and valley-dependent mass corrections that reshape the Berry curvature (BC) and shift the conditions for band inversion. By evaluating the quasienergy bands, BC, and spin- valley-resolved Chern numbers, we identify a sequence of light and electric field controlled topological transitions by gap closing. Depending on the Floquet coupling strength and the electric-field parameter, the system evolves between the equilibrium quantum spin Hall (QSH) state and a set of driven phases including spin-polarized quantum Hall insulator (S-QHI), band insulator (BI) and photo-induced quantum Hall insulator (P-QHI) regimes. The results establish 1T$^\prime$--MoS$_2$ as a tunable platform where circular driving selectively manipulates spin and valley degrees of freedom, enabling controlled access to non-equilibrium topological phases in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs).
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Mortezaei Nobahari

item.title: Engineering Fractional Topological Superconductors: Numerical Bogoliubov-de Gennes Analysis for Parafermion Realization in FCI-Superconductor Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2512.16025v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a pathway to engineer Z3 parafermion zero modes in fractional Chern insulator-superconductor heterostructures. Using numerical Bogoliubov-de Gennes calculations and edge-theory analysis, we demonstrate how realistic materials such as MoTe2/NbSe2 can host parafermionic excitations with experimentally accessible signatures, including fractional Josephson effects, localized zero modes, interferometry, and thermal transport. Our work outlines concrete strategies for experimentally accessing parafermionic excitations in FCI-superconductor heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Amire

item.title: Unconventional magnetoelectric conductivity and electrochemical response from dipole-like sources of Berry curvature
item.description: arXiv:2602.08844v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the longitudinal magnetoelectric conductivity and nonlinear electrochemical response (ECR) of three-dimensional nodal-ring semimetals, including vortex nodal-rings (VNRs) and $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric nodal-rings (PTNRs), together with three-band Hopf semimetals (HSMs), using the semiclassical Boltzmann formalism. The nodal-rings of the VNRs and PTNRs lie in the $k_z=0$ plane, whereas the nodal points of HSMs host isolated Berry-curvature (BC) dipoles with axes along the $k_z$ direction. In VNRs, such dipoles may be viewed as forming a continuous distribution along the nodal-ring, connecting the two classes of systems. For collinear electric and magnetic ($\mathcal{B}$) fields along the anisotropy axis $\boldsymbol {\hat{z}}$, the linear response is computed exactly and displays odd powers of $B_z$ for a single ring or node. For a two-node HSM with oppositely-oriented BC-dipole axes, these odd terms cancel in the sum. We analyse the nonlinear ECR, described by third-rank response tensors that relate the current to the combined action of an electric field and a chemical-potential gradient. The surviving tensor components are determined by the tilt direction of the bandstructure, and we obtain explicit results for simultaneous in-plane and axial tilts. A comparison of the three systems reveals a close correspondence between the responses of VNRs and HSMs, while PTNRs behave qualitatively differently. We attribute these similarities and differences to the topology of the BC field, namely dipole-like sources in VNRs and HSMs versus the ring-confined BC structure of PTNRs.
item.dc:creator: Ipsita Mandal

item.title: Disentangling Spin Pumping and Two-Magnon Scattering Contributions to Gilbert Damping in YIG/V Bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2605.29597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we investigate the magnetic damping and spin pumping response of YIG-based bilayers incorporating vanadium (V) as the normal metal layer via broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurements as a function of YIG thickness. We show that the apparent enhancement of the Gilbert damping in YIG/V bilayers cannot be solely attributed to spin pumping. Instead, two-magnon scattering (TMS) plays a dominant role in governing the thickness dependence of the damping in the nanometer regime. By applying a thickness-dependent damping model that accounts for both spin pumping and two-magnon scattering contributions, we successfully disentangle the different relaxation contributions. Our analysis reveals that neglecting two-magnon scattering leads to an overestimation of the spin-pumping contribution and consequently to unphysically large values of the effective spin-mixing conductance. After isolating the intrinsic spin pumping contribution, we extract a thickness-independent effective spin-mixing conductance of $g^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.33 \times 10^{18}~\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These findings provide a more accurate framework for quantifying spin transport parameters in FM/HM systems and emphasize the necessity of accounting for extrinsic damping mechanisms when interpreting spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect experiments.
item.dc:creator: S. Elkady, A. Tlais, H. Reslan, S. Isber, M. Haidar

item.title: Improving the Dynamic Range of Interacting Quantum Sensors via Optimized Quantum Control
item.description: arXiv:2505.04958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Interacting spin ensembles are promising platforms for quantum sensing, but spin-spin interactions can induce complex, nonmonotonic responses to external fields, limiting the dynamic range over which the fields can be estimated unambiguously. Here, we propose a quantum-circuit-learning-inspired method to improve the dynamic range of interacting quantum sensors using optimized global control fields. We consider an ensemble of dipole-coupled spins subjected to an inhomogeneous magnetic field generated by an electric current. By optimizing the global control fields applied during sensing, we train the expectation value of the collective magnetization to approximate a prescribed monotonic target function. We also introduce a penalty on the magnetization variance to account for measurement fluctuations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the optimized control can substantially enlarge the dynamic range compared with sensing without control. We further investigate the trade-off between dynamic range and estimation uncertainty and show that the variance penalty can reduce the uncertainty at the expense of dynamic range. These results demonstrate that learning-assisted global control provides a promising approach to improving the performance of interacting quantum sensors.
item.dc:creator: Yasuhiro Aota, Yuichiro Mori, Takahiko Satoh, Yuichiro Matsuzaki, Hideaki Kawaguchi

item.title: Kekul\'{e} Superconductivity Induced by Quantum Geometry in Haldane Phases
item.description: arXiv:2508.21791v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chiral two-dimensional electron gases, which capture the electronic properties of graphene and rhombohedral graphene systems, exhibit singular momentum-space vortices and are susceptible to interaction-induced topological Haldane phases. Here, we investigate pairing interactions in the inversion-symmetric Haldane phases of chiral two-dimensional electron gases. We demonstrate that the nontrivial band topology of the Haldane phases enhances intra-valley ($\Qq = \pm 2 \Kk_D$) pair susceptibility relative to inter-valley ($\Qq = 0$) pair susceptibility, favoring the emergence of a lattice-scale pair-density wave order. When longitudinal acoustic phonons mediate the pairing interaction, the system supports a chiral Kekul\`{e} superconducting order at low densities. At higher densities, the phase diagram depends on the parity of the Chern number $J$. For even parity, an s-wave Kekul\`{e} order appears, while for odd parity we find a $\Qq =0$ valley triplet chiral-$J$ and a valley singlet s-wave order at different densities. Our findings are relevant to superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene and Kagome metals.
item.dc:creator: Yafis Barlas, Fan Zhang, Enrico Rossi

item.title: Intrinsic non-Markovian magnetisation dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2512.07378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Memory effects are widespread in complex systems while evidence of non-Markovian dynamics in fundamental physical systems has been limited to specifically engineered cases. Here we report on the experimental observation of non-Markovian magnetisation dynamics in crystalline cobalt. Intense terahertz electromagnetic driving brings the system into a non-equilibrium state, and allows us to follow its magnetisation dynamics in real time at low temperatures. The response reveals a striking multi-peaked frequency spectrum that defies conventional descriptions. Using open quantum system theory we evidence that a non-Markovian memory kernel, arising from spin-phonon bath coupling, naturally explains both the spectral structure and its temperature dependence. Theoretical prediction of the spectrum is accomplished by simulating the non-Markovian Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, while analytics quantitatively determines the frequencies of three spectral peaks. The results demonstrate that intrinsic memory effects can emerge in a simple ferromagnet, opening new opportunities to explore and control non-Markovian dynamics in condensed-matter systems.
item.dc:creator: Felix Hartmann, Vivek Unikandanunni, Matias Bargheer, Eric E. Fullerton, Stefano Bonetti, Janet Anders

item.title: Operating a bistable qubit
item.description: arXiv:2605.03187v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parasitic two-level-system (TLS) defects limit the stability and performance of solid-state quantum processors. Their interaction with a qubit can cause discrete, stochastic shifts of the qubit frequency, making the qubit bistable. We experimentally demonstrate an adaptive protocol for operating a bistable qubit with high fidelity using a classical controller powered by a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Our "1-bit feedback" protocol estimates the qubit's bistable frequency and corrects the control frame using only one single-shot measurement, reaching the information limit set by the qubit's intrinsic entropy. We validate the protocol in a superconducting qubit by suppressing TLS-induced Ramsey beating, and deploy it to stabilize gate fidelities over time with approximately 136 kHz estimation bandwidth and a 77% error reduction. Our approach provides a simple, yet fundamentally efficient strategy for mitigating dephasing errors induced by strongly coupled TLS defects, and may enable the operation of large future qubit arrays suffering from few remaining, discrete instabilities.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Berritta, Jan A. Krzywda, Tom Dvir, Paul Buttles, Stanislav Eilhart, Jeroen Danon, Ferdinand Kuemmeth

item.title: Tunable non-Hermitian skin effect and topological phases in ladders with staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping
item.description: arXiv:2607.11454v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) and topological phases in a ladder model with staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping, consisting of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain coupled to a normal tight-binding chain. By tuning the system parameters, we show that the direction of the NHSE under open boundary conditions can be reversed and can even become energy dependent. The NHSE is further characterized by the spectral winding number under periodic boundary conditions. We also demonstrate that the interleg coupling significantly enlarges the topologically nontrivial parameter regime. Remarkably, there are two topological phases characterized by winding numbers $W=\pm1$, with the zero-energy topological edge modes residing on different sites in the two legs. Furthermore, increasing the nonreciprocity of the interleg hopping modifies the topological phase boundaries and eventually drives the system into a topologically trivial phase. Our results establish staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping as an effective mechanism for engineering both the non-Hermitian skin effect and topological phases in ladder systems.
item.dc:creator: Pu-Xuan Li, Qi-Bo Zeng

item.title: Eddy currents and current reversal in curved magnetic thin-film Josephson junctions
item.description: arXiv:2607.16399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Real-space geometric curvature in magnetic thin films introduces a controllable mechanism for tailoring the pathways of superconducting steady-state Josephson currents via the proximity effect. We present a generalized Green's function method for calculating diffusive transport in arbitrarily curved surfaces, and show how the competing mechanisms of curvature and distance regulate conversion between different superconducting pairings in a proximity-coupled ferromagnet. We show how this dictates the distribution of current density, with the possibility of curvature-controlled current density manipulation, induced eddy currents and current reversal.
item.dc:creator: Einar Skoglund, Maxim A. Tj{\o}tta, Sol H. Jacobsen

item.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25046v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

item.title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
item.description: arXiv:2610.34736v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation $\mathrm{(0.0086 \pm 0.0002) \mu_{B}/Mn}$ that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of $\mathrm{(291 \pm 2)\, K}$.
item.dc:creator: Servet Ozdemir, Ping-Luen Ho, Callum Brennan-Rich, Matthew Rogers, Philippa Shepley, Ahmet Yagmur, Ismet Gelen, Sehwan Song, Zabeada Aslam, Mannan Ali, Shelly Conroy, Sandrine Heutz, Gavin Burnell, B J Hickey

item.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
item.description: arXiv:2610.38704v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase and fixes the heat current along its edge. It has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that a calibrated combination of directional edge absorption weights determines $c$. A modulation of the edge couplings that travels along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra, and a static change of the same couplings measures the unknown probe normalization. Two harmonics then cancel the dependence on the edge state, so the estimator returns $c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory. A ratio of line weights with and without a vison gives the conformal spin of the Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb model, exact calculations recover $c=1/2$ and $h_\sigma=1/16$ to $10^{-5}$ and give $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins. Compiled into gate circuits on the physical spins of a square-lattice quantum simulator, the protocol returns $c$ within $5\%$ on 48 qubits. For stochastic gate errors it requires two-qubit error rates of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Ghosh

item.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03469v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $\pi$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.
item.dc:creator: Yves Rottstaedt, Andrei I. Pavlov, Alexander Shnirman, Yuval Gefen, Bernd Rosenow
